rationale: queens is a tiny, compute-bound recursive backtracking benchmark with small hot functions, no external input parsing, and simple integer arithmetic, so the priority is cheap, correctness-safe obfuscation that survives optimization rather than heavy transformation of cold code. SUB and SPLIT get high security/diversity weights with minimal cost/risk weights since instruction substitution and basic-block splitting are nearly free and safe on arithmetic-dominated code; BCF and IBR get moderate security weights paired with elevated runtime-cost weights so the compiler applies them selectively to the hot solver path (bogus loops and indirect branches compound quickly in a recursive search); FLA keeps a decent security weight but the highest runtime cost and a notable correctness risk because flattening recursive backtracking control flow both slows the inner loop and risks state-machine miscompilation; ICALL and IGV are weighted toward being disabled since queens has few indirect-call or interprocedural sites to disguise, making their overhead and risk unjustified.
